title: Degradation triage diary - May 15 2029
content:
Ops diary: degradation triage and handoff notes

Summary:
This week’s diary records a set of small-to-medium degradations across the hosted API (eu-west, us-west), SLO impact and immediate mitigations. No customer data was exposed. Primary learning: prefix KV cache pressure combined with a new batching policy caused transient tail-latency spikes for short-chat workloads.

Incidents (short chronology):
1) 2029-05-13 03:10–03:42 UTC — INF-3421: short-chat tail latency spike (p99 from 380ms -> 2.4s) affecting eu-west region for ~32 minutes.
   - Symptoms: increased p95/p99 on chat routes, backlog in request queue, several 503s in proxy due to queue saturation.
   - Root cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction churn after model variant roll (v1.9 -> v1.9-quant) + aggressive batch window shortening.
   - Immediate mitigations: rolled back batch window to previous policy (team: serving-runtime), restarted proxy pool nodes in eu-west (SRE), bumped autoscale thresholds to tolerate increased CPU during warmup.
   - Follow-ups: INF-3421 assigned to Armand (investigate cache churn), INF-3429 created for telemetry enhancement.

2) 2029-05-14 11:50–12:06 UTC — degraded embeddings ingestion (background worker backlog) in us-west.
   - Symptoms: ingestion lag increased from ~1 minute to ~12 minutes; no client-facing errors but search freshness impacted.
   - Cause: side-effect of autoscaler cooldown parameter change on worker pool; pods scaled down too aggressively during a low-traffic window, then could not scale back fast enough when ingestion burst arrived.
   - Mitigation: temporarily set min-replicas to 3 and lowered scaleDownDelay.
   - Follow-ups: update autoscale playbook and add a synthetic ingestion heartbeat.

SLO snapshot (as of 2029-05-15 06:00 UTC):
- Chat generation availability SLO (99.9% monthly): current month burn 0.17% (on track).
- Chat latency SLO (p95 < 500ms): weekly burn spike after INF-3421; daily dip recovered after rollback.
- Embeddings freshness SLO (90% within 2 minutes): temporary breach window during us-west event.

Telemetry notes and gaps:
- We lack fine-grained KV cache eviction counters per-model-variant; only host-level counts available. Added INF-3429 to add per-variant eviction and cache hit-ratio metrics.
- Need better correlation between batching-window config changes and per-route latency; opened a PR to tag batch-window values in request traces (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1182).

On-call handoff (for next 24h):
- Key watchpoints: eu-west chat p95/p99; worker queue length for embeddings us-west; alert INF-HighTailLatency threshold 9 -> 7 (tighter until follow-ups complete).
- Active tickets to mention during handoff: JIRA-INF-3421 (investigation), JIRA-INF-3429 (telemetry), JIRA-OPS-2110 (autoscaler tuning).
- Suggested immediate steps for oncall: if p99 > 1.5s for >5m -> escalate to serving-runtime pager and run cache-warmup script (runbook link in artifacts). If worker backlog > 10k -> set min-replicas and contact infra for node warmup.

Action items and owners (short):
- Armand Silva: deep dive on KV cache churn and eviction patterns (JIRA-INF-3421). Due 2029-05-20.
- Nina Patel: add per-variant cache metrics + dashboard panel (JIRA-INF-3429). Due 2029-05-18.
- Owen Martinez: revert and evaluate recent autoscale cooldown changes; propose safe defaults and synthetic heartbeat test (JIRA-OPS-2110). Due 2029-05-17.
- Leah Ko (SRE): add a short playbook subsection for "warmup window after model variant roll" and publish to runbooks. Due 2029-05-16.

Operational observations and quick experiments:
- Canary tweak: we tested increasing the batch-window for short-chat routes by 30ms during the eu-west rollback; p95 improved ~60ms while cost per-token rose <1.5%. This is a candidate for a controlled experiment in staging.
- Autoscaler: observed that scale-up latency for worker pods is correlated with image-pull times on low-util nodes; propose moving frequently-scaling worker images to a small pre-warmed node pool.

Risks and open questions:
- If we continue rolling model variants without per-variant cache telemetry, regressions will be harder to triage quickly.
- Quantized variant memory behavior differs; need an explicit checklist for variant rollouts (KV cache impact, expected memory footprint, backoff config).

Meeting notes (standup highlights):
- 2029-05-15 SRE standup: serving-runtime will ship a safe toggle for batch-window; infra prioritized pre-warm node pool; product-aware risk review scheduled 2029-05-17.
- Action: Leah to present a 10-minute incident walkthrough in next engineering all-hands.

Useful links:
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/kv-cache-runbook
- Latency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/serving-latency-dashboard
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1182

Handoff summary for next oncall (copy to Slack #sre-oncall):
- Short: monitor eu-west chat p95/p99 closely; if tail spikes, rollback batch-window (playbook) and notify serving-runtime. Watch embeddings worker queue in us-west; if backlog persists > 10 minutes, enforce min-replicas=3 and page infra.

Notes to self:
- Keep list of small experiments that trade a small cost increase for meaningful p95 gains; these are the fastest wins for PLG growth metrics.
- Record follow-up learning in a short post-incident note after Armand's dive.

End of diary entry.
